stories.title: HMRC to send £70 refund letters to one million low earners
stories.summary: HMRC will write to approximately one million people, mostly women, explaining their eligibility for top-up pension tax relief payments averaging £70. Recipients are low earners who missed out due to their employer's 'Net Pay Arrangement' pension scheme and will be contacted automatically over the coming months.

stories.title: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax: Scheduled Service Maintenance
stories.summary: HMRC has published a service availability notice for Making Tax Digital for Income Tax, with scheduled maintenance planned from 5pm Friday 11 September to 1pm Tuesday 15 September 2026. A previous service issue with viewing accounts has been resolved.

stories.title: Minister Makes Statement on South Coast Anti-Immigration Protests
stories.summary: Minister for Policing Sarah Jones MP gave an oral statement to Parliament about public order following anti-immigration protests at Dover and Portsmouth over the weekend, where around 150 individuals blocked the Port of Dover and over 200 protesters tried to stop coaches carrying asylum seekers. Police used batons and PAVA spray in Portsmouth; investigations are ongoing.

stories.title: Number of Asylum Seekers in Hotels Halves in a Year
stories.summary: The number of asylum seekers accommodated in UK hotels has halved over the past year, reflecting the government's efforts to reduce reliance on hotel accommodation for asylum seekers.

stories.title: Forty Children Missing from UK Asylum Hotels Still Not Found
stories.summary: Forty children who were reported missing from UK asylum hotels remain unaccounted for, raising ongoing concerns about the safety and oversight of asylum seeker accommodation.

stories.title: UK Announces Trade Ban on Goods from Illegal Israeli Settlements
stories.summary: Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband is making a statement to Parliament today to announce a UK ban on trade in goods and some services from illegal Israeli settlements, as part of a broader reset of UK-Israel relations. The move aims to reassert support for a two-state solution and has drawn criticism from the US and Israel.

stories.title: FCDO Updates UK Sanctions List: ISIL and Al-Qaeda
stories.summary: The FCDO updated the UK Sanctions List on 7 September 2026 under the ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaeda regime, imposing asset freezes, arms embargoes and travel bans on newly listed individuals.

agencies.name: DEFRA
agencies.description: Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs

stories.title: UK Cities Most Vulnerable to Extreme Heat Revealed
stories.summary: Research by Ordnance Survey, the Met Office and 4 Earth Intelligence has created a heat vulnerability index for all 71 chartered cities in Great Britain, finding Portsmouth is the most vulnerable now and into the future. The research follows this summer being provisionally the UK's hottest on record, with almost two-thirds of cities projected to reach the most severe heat vulnerability level by the end of the century.

stories.title: Government Responds to Animal Sentience Committee on Glue Traps Act
stories.summary: DEFRA has published the government's formal response to the Animal Sentience Committee's views on the Glue Traps (Offences) Act 2022, addressing the committee's recommendations on the treatment of animals as sentient beings under the legislation.

stories.title: UK Opens New Defence Centre in Poland to Bolster NATO Air Defences
stories.summary: Minister for Defence Readiness Luke Pollard MP opened a new MBDA missile logistics facility in Czosnów, Poland, supporting Poland's PILICA+ integrated air defence network. The centre will support over 400 UK jobs in Bristol, Stevenage and Bolton while reinforcing NATO's eastern flank against Russian aggression.

stories.title: New £7.8bn UK National Space Strategy Strengthens Defence and Security
stories.summary: The new National Space Strategy, jointly launched with BIST today, includes £880m for space control and intelligence capabilities and £2.8bn for satellite connectivity including the SKYNET defence communications programme. It replaces the 2021 National Space Strategy and is backed by record investment until 2030.

stories.title: National Armaments Director Appoints New Chief Financial Officer
stories.summary: The National Armaments Director has appointed Ian Brimicombe as the new Chief Financial Officer for the NAD Group, strengthening financial leadership for the UK's defence procurement body.

agencies.name: BIST
agencies.description: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

stories.title: UK Launches £7.8bn National Space Strategy
stories.summary: Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds and Defence Secretary Wes Streeting jointly launched the UK's first cross-government National Space Strategy today, backed by £7.8bn investment until 2030. The strategy covers satellite communications, in-orbit servicing, space domain awareness and assured access to space, aiming to grow the UK space sector to £18.6bn and support 55,000 skilled jobs.

stories.title: Architect of UK's AI Policy Resigns over Anthropic Conflict of Interest
stories.summary: Matt Clifford, chair of the government's Advanced Research and Invention Agency (Aria), has stepped down after taking a full-time job at Anthropic, following concerns from senior MPs about a 'clear conflict of interest'. He will remain in post until 6 November with safeguards in place.

stories.title: Smart Data Challenge Prize: Insights and Outcomes Published
stories.summary: BIST published the findings and outcomes from the Smart Data Challenge Prize, an initiative exploring how smart data access can drive innovation. The report highlights significant insights from challenge participants.

stories.title: 'Mistrust' of Palantir May Affect NHS Research, Warns Health Minister
stories.summary: Health Innovation Minister James Frith has warned that public mistrust of Palantir could affect people's willingness to share medical data with the NHS, after 60,000 additional patients withdrew their data in just two months. The government is reviewing Palantir's £330m contract for the NHS federated data platform, and has signalled that use of the platform is not mandatory for trusts.

stories.title: Wolverhampton and Walsall NHS Trusts Deploy AI Ambient Voice Technology
stories.summary: NHS trusts in Wolverhampton and Walsall have deployed Heidi, an AI-powered Ambient Voice Technology (AVT) system, designed to reduce administrative burden on clinicians during medical consultations by automatically transcribing and structuring consultation notes.

stories.title: Sleep App Cough Data Could Give Early Warning of Respiratory Illness
stories.summary: Research by Sleep Cycle has found that cough data collected passively through a sleep app could provide early warning of rising respiratory illnesses, including flu and COVID-19, offering potential applications for NHS pandemic preparedness and population health monitoring.

stories.title: Royal Mail's Universal Service Obligation Failure Raised via Urgent Parliamentary Question
stories.summary: An urgent question was raised in Parliament today concerning Royal Mail's failure to meet its Universal Service Obligation, which requires delivery of letters on at least five days a week across the UK. The question followed ongoing concerns about postal delivery performance standards.
